quote: Rotork (ROR LN) - is a UK-based, market-leading global provider of mission-critical intelligent flow control solutions (actuators, valves and associated instrumentation) for oil and gas, water and wastewater, power, and chemical process applications, serving customers in more than 170 countries through a global network of manufacturing and service locations. Rotork's products sit deep inside customers' plants and pipelines in applications where failure is simply not an option, and roughly half of group revenue is generated from a high-margin aftermarket service and spares business tied to a large installed base. This combination of mission-criticality and recurring revenue has historically supported EBIT margins in the low-to-mid 20's and 30%+ ROIC. Shares surged during the month after Swiss industrial technology group ABB agreed to acquire Rotork in an all-cash bid at 503 pence per share, valuing the business at an enterprise value of approximately US$5.5 billion - a premium of 70% to Rotork's last traded price. We had held Rotork on the view that the market was persistently underpricing a high-return, aftermarket-driven business relative to its through-cycle earnings power. ABB's willingness to pay a full cash premium to take the business private is a vindication of that view rather than a surprise, and a timely reminder that disciplined, moat-quality small caps continue to attract genuine strategic and financial buyers even in a market currently fixated on AI-linked narratives.

headline: Spheria maintains Santos position at 7x FY26 EV/EBIT, viewing the post-Iran peace deal share price weakness as an attractive entry into a growing cash flow story
reasoning: Santos is Australia's second-largest independent oil and gas producer with a low-cost, long-life upstream portfolio anchored by LNG across Australia, PNG, Timor-Leste and Alaska. Management targets an all-in free cash flow breakeven of US$45–$50/bbl and aims to return at least 60% of FCF to shareholders from 2026, with Barossa LNG and Pikka Oil projects expected to lift group output by ~15–27% in 2026. Shares fell in June following confirmation of a US-Iran peace framework which removed the geopolitical risk premium from oil prices. However, Spheria believes ongoing regional instability reinforces the importance of energy security and diversifying supply away from the Middle East, enhancing the strategic value of Santos's portfolio. At 7x FY26 EV/EBIT, with output stepping up and capex rolling off, Spheria views the valuation as increasingly attractive.
quote: Santos (STO AU) - is Australia's second-largest independent oil and gas producer, with a portfolio spanning LNG, domestic gas, crude oil and condensate across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and Alaska. Santos operates a low-cost, long-life upstream portfolio anchored by LNG, with interests in PNG LNG, Gladstone LNG and Darwin LNG providing exposure to Asian gas demand alongside domestic Cooper Basin and Western Australian supply. Management runs the business to an all-in free cash flow breakeven of US$45 to US$50 per barrel and targets returning at least 60% of free cash flow to shareholders from 2026. Its Barossa LNG and Pikka Oil (Alaska) projects are ramping up and are expected to lift group output by roughly 15% to 27% in 2026, moving Santos from a heavy capital investment phase into stronger cash generation. The shares fell during June following confirmation of a peace framework between the United States and Iran, which removed much of the geopolitical risk premium from oil prices and in turn weighed on Santos. Nevertheless, we believe that ongoing regional instability reinforces the importance of energy security and the need to diversify energy supply away from the Middle East, enhancing the strategic value of Santos's portfolio. Santos trades on 7x FY26 EV/EBIT, a multiple that should look increasingly attractive as Barossa and Pikka reach full production.

headline: Spheria maintains overweight in Karoon Energy despite 26% monthly fall, arguing the market has overreacted to Who Dat production issues while Bauna — the key asset — is fully back online
reasoning: Karoon fell 26% in the month, driven by an oil price decline and a downward revision to CY26 production guidance from 8.1-9.2 MMboe to 7.2-8.2 MMboe due to subsea equipment failure at the Who Dat field in the Gulf of Mexico, with full repairs not expected until 2027. However, Spheria argues the market has overreacted because Who Dat represents only approximately 25% of normalised group production. Bauna in Brazil — which represents nearly 50% of company production — is now fully back online and commands a higher oil price premium. quote: Karoon Energy (KAR.ASX) returned -26% during the month, driven by both a fall in oil prices and a company-specific trading update. The company revised CY26 production guidance from 8.1-9.2 MMboe to 7.2-8.2 MMboe, due to lower production at its Who Dat field in the Gulf of Mexico. A piece of subsea equipment failed at one of Who Dat's key production points, and the operator now doesn't expect it to be fully repaired until 2027, meaning part of the field will produce well below its normal run rate. Two smaller wells due to come online later this year will help offset some of the shortfall, but not enough to close the gap entirely. Importantly, Karoon's main oil well at its Bauna Project is now fully back online. This well represents nearly 50% of the company's production in Brazil. We feel the market has overreacted to the issues at Who Dat, given it represents approximately 25% of normalised group production. Bauna is far more important, given it is most of group production and commands a higher premium for its oil. Importantly, it is also now past its capex hump and despite the higher spending, management announced a further share buyback of up to 10% of shares on issue - reflecting confidence in the company's overall cash flows and balance sheet strength.

headline: Warns of a thematically concentrated AI-driven market running on narrative rather than arithmetic, with elevated yields and deteriorating rates outlook compounding risk
reasoning: Spheria observes that 2026 market energy has shifted almost entirely to AI-connected themes, mirroring 2025's enthusiasm for resources and gold, which has since faded. The rates picture has deteriorated, with yields staying elevated and expectations swinging toward further rate rises, yet markets continue to sit at or near all-time highs. Spheria believes markets that shrug off tighter policy while at all-time highs tend to be running on narrative rather than arithmetic, and describes the current environment as hostile for a valuation-disciplined approach. quote: Every cycle produces a stock, or in this case a person, that becomes shorthand for the market's mood. SpaceX's IPO in June, the largest listing on record, briefly pushed Elon Musk past a trillion dollars in net worth, a threshold no individual had crossed before... A fortune that can cross the trillion-dollar line twice in a month reveals less about wealth itself than about the price the market is currently willing to pay for a compelling narrative. That episode fits neatly within the broader theme defining 2026. Last year's enthusiasm centered on resources, gold in particular, which now sits well off its highs as its macro underpinnings look tired. This year the energy has shifted almost entirely to anything connected to artificial intelligence. The technological shift is real, and the Fund holds businesses positioned to benefit from it, so the concern isn't with the theme itself but with its reach. Against that, the rates picture has deteriorated, with yields staying elevated and expectations swinging decisively toward further rate rises. Markets that shrug off tighter policy while sitting at or near all-time highs tend, in our experience, to be running on narrative rather than arithmetic.

quote: Bapcor (BAP) experienced a weak performance in May, exacerbated by a profit downgrade announced mid-month amid deteriorating macroeconomic conditions. This is a complex situation that requires conviction. Significant wage inflation, elevated oil and fuel prices, and their adverse impact on car servicing activity and product demand have created a challenging operating environment. The balance sheet is still under repair, which is limiting capital flexibility and potentially requiring divestments in what remains a buyer's market. That said, several positive elements are emerging. The macro headwinds are expected to moderate over time, and the new CEO, Chris Wilesmith – an experienced aftermarket parts executive from Supercheap Auto – has made an encouraging start to the turnaround since joining in December. Early sales data prior to the US-Iran conflict, together with positive feedback from our supplier discussions, point to improving momentum under his leadership. The Trade division, representing approximately 35% of group sales, remains the standout asset. We estimate it generates revenue of around $800m and, at a conservative mid-cycle EBIT margin of 10%, this business alone – operating in an effective duopoly with Repco (GPC) – is worth in excess of $800m and potentially more than $1 billion. This compares to BAP's current EV of only $450m. The retail brands present a more challenging turnaround, although initial signs of market share gains are evident in the mid-May release. Potential divestment of selected wholesale and specialist businesses would provide further scope for debt reduction. Pro-forma net debt of $195m following the equity raising has already declined to $168m. Chris is successfully attracting talent back into the organisation, and we view him as the pivotal factor in the recovery. Given its attractive Trade platform, Bapcor also presents as an obvious target for private equity or a strategic buyer such as US-listed O'Reilly Automotive (~$75 billion market cap), which is a close mirror image of the group in the US market.

Spheria acknowledges the new wave of technological advancement is one not seen in decades and the portfolio has benefited from select exposure, but remains cautious about the narrowness of what is driving market returns. The firm warns of the well-worn dynamic where momentum attracts capital, capital validates momentum, and the thematic becomes the market. Spheria will not chase prices that cannot be justified by discounted cash flows. The firm is particularly cautious on some ascribed Australian small-cap valuations that have filtered through from the AI theme.
quote: 2026 has instead seen the aggressive rise of AI investing. Whilst the theme has been building for several years, the intensity of capital being directed toward it this year has been remarkable. Businesses that were barely known by the masses three years ago - OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX - are now commanding valuations in the hundreds of billions, and any company perceived as a beneficiary has seen its share price follow. We acknowledge the new wave of technological advancement is one not seen in decades and our portfolio has benefited from select exposure to it. But we remain cautious on some of the ascribed Australian small-cap valuations that have filtered through, and more broadly on the narrowness of what is driving market returns. This is the well-worn dynamic we have seen repeatedly: momentum attracts capital, capital validates momentum, and before long the thematic becomes the market. Our discipline remains unchanged. We will not chase prices that cannot be justified by discounted cash flows, regardless of how compelling the narrative appears in the moment.
episode_title: Spheria Global Opportunities Fund Report May 2026

headline: Spheria holds and modestly adds to Hemnet despite persistent weakness, arguing real estate portals are harder to disrupt by AI than feared
reasoning: Hemnet, the dominant Swedish real estate portal, has been a significant detractor since peaking in February 2025. Despite this, Spheria has added modestly to the position, arguing that real estate is a high-stakes transaction where buyers cannot afford to miss listings and sellers cannot afford to miss buyers. Less than 1% of traffic currently comes from AI chatbots, and agents benefit greatly from the status quo, reducing the likelihood of voluntary disruption. Spheria acknowledges AI as a genuine risk but concludes real estate portals will likely prove harder to disrupt than markets fear.
quote: Despite the obvious uncertainty attaching to this question, we remain holders of HEM and have added modestly to the position in recent months. Our thinking is as follows: Real estate is a 'high stakes' transaction. Transacting in a property is often the biggest transaction of the buyer and the seller's lives. The buyer cannot afford to miss any listings in their search, and the seller cannot afford to miss any buyers, as the cost of doing so could dwarf the cost of the listing. HEM is developing vertical Ai features. To the extent that the risk to the business is an app that sits inside ChatGPT and the other Ai chatbots, HEM seems highly likely to be that app. HEM has high brand recognition, with very high (70-90%) levels of direct and organic traffic flows, evidence of embedded agent and consumer behaviours and habits. Today well less than 1% of HEM's traffic comes from Ai chatbots. If this grows and prospective buyers wish to begin their purchase journey on an Ai chatbot, HEM will be part of that in the same way that it uses Google as a marketing funnel today.

headline: Spheria holds overweight in USLM and would add further on share price weakness, citing highly favourable industry structure and strong cash generation
reasoning: USLM is an integrated manufacturer of lime and limestone products with owned long-life quarries and mines, serving primarily steel manufacturing and construction markets. The lime industry is highly regionalised, with USLM and competitor Lhoist together serving the central US and Texan markets, creating a duopoly-like structure that supports strong cash flows and returns. In Q3, strength in construction tied to large data-centre projects is offsetting weakness in oil and gas services volumes, and price growth remains robust at +5%. Spheria views USLM as a high-quality business operating within a highly favourable industry structure and states they would gladly add further to the position should the share price continue to soften materially from current levels.
quote: USLM is a highly cash generative, high returning business with a net cash balance sheet. As is almost always the case, it's the industry structure that's decisive in giving rise to these characteristics. Specifically, the lime industry is highly regionalised, with its heavy, low value per tonne nature making it costly to transport long distances. Consequently, there tends to be 2 or 3 primary competitors in each region, as is the case with USLM & its main competitor, Lhoist, which together serve the central US and Texan markets. Whilst competing sources of lime (from say, Mexico) do find their way into the market from time to time, not only is the landed cost higher but there's also a quality trade-off. So as long as USLM (and Lhoist) don't abuse their privileged market position, the opportunity to continue to generate strong cash flows and returns should persist long into the future. USLM is a high-quality business operating within a highly favourable industry structure. We will gladly add further to the position should the share price continue to soften materially from current levels.

headline: Spheria defends overweight in Sapiens despite near-term revenue growth slowdown, citing 30% upside to mid-cycle valuation at just 11.5x EBITA
reasoning: Sapiens is a global insurance software business operating in a $40bn+ addressable market, with only half of 2,500 global insurers having migrated off legacy systems. Organic revenue growth has slowed from a consistent 6-9% to near zero due to macro-driven customer deferrals, increased US P&C competition, and a near-term revenue drag from cloud migration of existing clients converting licence payments to annuities. Spheria believes this is a transitory period: the company is integrating AI to differentiate, expanding cross-sell and L&A focus, and building system integrator channels. Cloud delivery will ultimately improve business quality via more recurring revenue, lower support costs, and automatic updates. At 11.5x EBITA with a net cash balance sheet, Spheria sees 30% upside to its through-the-cycle valuation.
quote: We believe the market is being short-sighted and that this will transpire to be a transitory period of low growth for SPNS. Firstly, the company is responding to the competitive challenge in the US, actively integrating Ai into its product to differentiate itself, expanding cross-sell initiatives (most customers only have 1 product), enhancing the focus on L&A (where competition is less intense) and it continues to build out system integrator partnerships globally as an entirely new channel to market for the group; Secondly, whilst the transition to the cloud impacts near term earnings, ultimately business quality improves dramatically as cloud delivered software means more recurring revenue (improved financial stability and valued highly by the market), lower support costs, whilst the customer simultaneously reduces its IT hardware spend and receives automatic updates; and Lastly, the macroeconomic uncertainty will pass, as it always does. SPNS now trades on just 11.5x EBITA, has a net cash balance sheet, and offers 30% upside to our fundamental, through the cycle valuation.

quote: Ferguson is the market leader in the U.S. wholesale distribution of plumbing, HVAC, and waterworks products. The company plays a critical role in connecting a large and fragmented supplier base with an even broader and more fragmented customer base. Notably, Ferguson is the only major distributor that's expanding and enhancing its distribution center capabilities—a key differentiator that strengthens its competitive moat versus its fragmented and franchise-heavy competitors. While deflationary pressures have weighed on earnings since early 2024, 3Q FY24 marked a turning point, with price inflation picking up for the first time since late 2023 and exceeding expectations. This supported a re-rating in Ferguson's share price, driven in part by stronger-than-expected commodity prices and improving trends in finished goods. We are particularly positive on Ferguson's exposure to HVAC and waterworks, which have helped to deliver five consecutive quarters of positive volume growth. In addition, U.S. onshoring remains a strong tailwind. Even after its recent rally, the stock trades on just 17x FY26 EBIT, which is more than fair for a market leader that continues to gain market share and generate returns north of 30%.

headline: Spheria retains Accelleron as a core holding after a 50%+ rebound, viewing it as fairly priced at 19x FY26 EBITA but well-supported by execution, balance sheet strength and multiple tailwinds
reasoning: Accelleron is the Swiss-based global leader in off-highway turbochargers for merchant marine and energy markets, with a mission-critical product that reduces fuel consumption and emissions. Over 50% of revenue comes from the merchant marine sector and 75% of group revenue is from servicing the existing fleet, providing resilience against short-term trade disruptions. The stock rebounded over 50% from tariff-related lows partly due to tariff negotiation progress and the strengthening Swiss franc (which benefits the company translationally and transactionally given ~50% of revenue is in CHF). Additional tailwinds include new IMO climate regulations from October 2025 and datacentre demand for backup and baseload power. At 19x FY26 EBITA the stock is seen as fairly priced but the company is gaining share, broadening its product suite, and generating phenomenal cash flow and returns.
quote: With the benefit of hindsight this would have been a great buying opportunity, with the stock rebounding over 50% since that time to make new highs. The reasons for this appear to be twofold. Firstly since 'Liberation Day' (2nd April), markets have breathed a long and collective sigh of relief as the US approach to tariff negotiations has inclined towards compromise. Over 50% of Accelleron's revenue comes from selling turbochargers and associated services to the merchant marine industry, so a reduction in global trade would clearly be unhelpful for the business. Having said that, the shorter-term impact would be modest given 75% of group revenue comes from servicing the existing fleet of turbochargers and the shipyards are book through at least 2027-28, meaning that turbocharger deliveries for newbuilds will continue regardless of short-term trade trends. The other factor driving Accelleron's recent bounce is the strength of the Swiss franc. Around 50% of its revenue negotiated, priced and settled in Swiss francs, which has rallied ~15% off the lows from earlier this year. As the company reports in USD, this will benefit the company from both a transactional and translational standpoint. Further, in April the IMO (International Maritime Organisation) announced a tightening of its climate regulations from October 2025 where fleet owners with aggregate emissions in excess of a predefined limit must pay into the IMO's Net Zero Fund. This, along with datacentre demand for both backup and baseload power, provide further tailwinds for Accelleron's business. Following the recent rally the stock is looking more fairly priced at 19x FY26 EBITA. Having said that the company is executing well, outperforming ours and the market's expectations as it gains share in turbochargers and broadens its product suite into new and growing TAMs. The balance sheet is strong and its cash flow and returns are phenomenal, and as such it remains a core holding in the Fund.

headline: Spheria adds to Hemnet position on 25% price decline, viewing regulatory concerns as overstated and valuation highly attractive at 26x FY26 EBITA.
reasoning: Hemnet's share price declined 25% during the quarter and over 30% from its February peak, driven by a weak listings environment and concerns from the Swedish Competition Authority and Real Estate Agency Inspectorate over market dominance and agent remuneration. Spheria views these concerns as overstated: 9 out of 10 Swedish homes were advertised on Hemnet in 2024, unchanged for five years, and no formal investigation has been confirmed. The fund sees Hemnet as early in the journey of rebalancing value capture away from agents toward the portal, and notes that forced removal of agent commissions could actually boost earnings. Following the selloff, the stock trades at 26x FY26 EBITA, which Spheria considers very attractive for a market-leading portal with strong network effects, strong cash generation, and capital return via dividends and buybacks. Spheria used the weakness to add to the position.
quote: Following the recent sell-off, the stock trades on an FY26 EBITA multiple of 26x, which is very attractive for a market leading real estate portal with strong network effects, generating strong cash flow and returning capital to shareholders via dividends and share buybacks. We are strongly of the view that the amount of value captured by real estate portals versus real estate agents is grossly disproportionate in favour of the agents and that Hemnet is very early on the journey of rebalancing this equation. The Real Estate Agency Inspectorate concerns over Hemnet's agent remuneration structure may perversely be a positive for the company. It is our view that the strength of Hemnet's network effects is such that there's little need to pay agent commissions, so having them forcibly reduced or removed would boost earnings without impacting market share.

headline: Spheria remains optimistic on Eagle Materials at 11x EBIT, citing high-quality low-cost assets, structural supply tightness, and bipartisan infrastructure spending tailwinds.
reasoning: Eagle Materials is a US manufacturer of cement and gypsum wallboard with operating margins and returns consistently above 20%, driven by vertical integration into low-cost lime and gypsum mining reserves. Synthetic gypsum supply has structurally tightened as US coal-fired power plants have more than halved in the past decade, reducing a key alternative input. On the cement side, regulatory burdens and community resistance make capacity additions rare, keeping supply and demand finely balanced. Bipartisan support for large public infrastructure spending should drive cement demand growth over the next 2-3 years, while a rebound in single-family home construction as interest rates ease should spur gypsum wallboard demand. Despite this quality, Eagle trades at a very modest 11x EBIT, which Spheria considers far too cheap, and they remain happy and optimistic holders.
quote: Eagle Materials is a US manufacturer of heavy construction materials, primarily cement and gypsum wallboard. On the face of it this might sound like a dull and commoditized business where you'd expect to find high levels of competition and little scope for excess returns. One look at Eagle's financial accounts tells you that you'd be mistaken, with operating margins and returns both consistently north of 20%. A number of factors give us confidence that this can be sustained or even improved upon. Firstly, Eagle is vertically integrated into both the mining of lime and gypsum, where they have the advantage of long-life, low-cost reserves. These inputs ensure the cost-competitiveness of their manufacturing plants versus much higher cost imports. Secondly, gypsum supply has structurally tightened in recent years, with synthetic gypsum – previously a viable alternative to natural gypsum – having dwindled in availability with the number of US coal-fired power plants more than halving in the past decade. Similarly on the cement side, capacity additions are a rarity owing to a burdensome regulatory environment and a reluctance from local communities to host new cement plants in their neighborhoods. All of this means that supply and demand are finely balanced for Eagle's key products, with future demand increases likely to translate directly into commensurate increases in price and margins. On the demand side, bipartisan support for large public infrastructure spending should fuel growth in the demand for cement over the next 2-3yrs, whilst a rebound in single-family home construction as interest rates ease will ultimately spur gypsum wallboard demand. With one of the highest quality (low cost) portfolios of assets in the building materials space that we've come across, Eagle currently trades on a very modest 11x EBIT. This is far too cheap, and we remain happy and optimistic holders of the business.

quote: LKQ is a large supplier of auto parts to collision repairers in the US and mechanics in Europe. The risk/ reward equation for LKQ is highly favourable as it is trading on a low EBIT multiple of 11x with cyclically depressed earnings. As the rate of vehicle insurance premium inflation subsides and used car prices firm, vehicles owners will become more inclined to repair their vehicles. This will drive a return to consistent mid-single-digit revenue growth, higher earnings growth and ultimately strong returns for the Fund.

headline: Spheria maintains Zuken as a core holding, seeing significant upside given dominant EDA market position and a valuation of just 10.5x EBIT versus Altium's 80x+ acquisition multiple
reasoning: Zuken is the dominant electronic design automation software player in Japan with 80% market share and ~20% international market share, operating in a consolidated global industry. The company benefits from powerful structural growth drivers including consumer electronics proliferation, EV/ADAS adoption, and industrial automation. Its competitive moat derives from 45 years of accumulated development code, component libraries, and tools that are extremely difficult to replicate. Despite this, the stock trades at only 10.5x FY26 EBIT, a stark discount to peer Altium which was acquired at over 80x EBIT. In FY25, Zuken grew revenue 10%, maintained margins while investing 13% of sales in R&D, generated free cash flow in excess of net profit, returned over Y5b to shareholders, and holds Y34b (~30% of market cap) in net cash.
quote: Zuken is a leading global software player in electronic design automation for printed circuit board and circuit design solutions. Its main end markets are automotive and consumer electronics, along with industrial machinery, medical devices, rail and aeronautical. The industry is exposed to powerful GDP+ growth drivers, including the proliferation of consumer electronics, the rise of EV's and ADAS (advanced driver-assistance systems) and industrial automation. Zuken is the dominant player in Japan with 80% market share and has material scope to grow internationally where it has ~20% market share. Industry structure is favourable with just a handful of players dominating globally. Zuken's strong market position is a function of its 45 years of development code, component libraries and associated tools, all of which are very hard to replicate. Despite all of this, the stock trades on a mere Forecast FY 26 multiple of 10.5x EBIT, even after outperforming strongly in the quarter. In stark contrast, competitor Altium was acquired in 2024 by Japanese manufacturing firm Renesas on an EBIT multiple north of 80x. Zuken remains a core holding in the portfolio and we continue to see plenty of upside to the current share price.

headline: Holding at ~20x EBIT as disruptive cross-border payments infrastructure with 20%+ revenue growth and net cash balance sheet
reasoning: Wise is displacing slow and expensive bank-based cross-border transfers, with over two-thirds of cross-border transfers still going through banks, providing significant runway for market share gains. Its competitive moat lies in 850+ software engineers building in-country connections and licensing that drives cost and speed advantages. Management is executing a 'land-grab' strategy by passing scale benefits to customers via lower prices, reinforcing rapid growth and further unit cost reductions. Notably, 50% of transaction volume is already facilitated by moving money between Wise customers without leaving the country, reducing execution costs and widening the moat as the network grows. The company is generating revenue growth in excess of 20% per annum with even stronger profit growth, holds a net cash balance sheet, and trades at approximately 20x EBIT. Spheria visited Wise in London, where management laid out a vision of becoming the network for international payment transfers, already signing up Morgan Stanley as a customer.
quote: Wise is a disruptive global technology company that is building out the infrastructure to facilitate money transfers and provide multi-currency accounts to individuals and businesses. Wise is transforming the markets in which it operates, displacing slow, expensive and opaque offerings from large banks. Over two thirds of cross-border transfers are still done through the banks, providing ample scope for continued market share gains. Wise's competitive advantage lies in its infrastructure, with its 850+ software engineers and associated staff who together are responsible for establishing the in-country connections and licensing that helps to drive its cost and speed advantage. In addition, Wise management is intelligently executing somewhat of a 'land-grab' strategy by passing the benefits of its scale back to its customers in the form of reduced prices. This underpins the group's rapid growth, which in turn lowers its unit costs and further drives growth. By way of example, 50% of Wise's current transaction volume is facilitated by moving money between Wise customers, whereby the money doesn't actually leave the country, thus reducing execution costs. The bigger Wise gets, the more this percentage will increase, the greater its competitive moat.

quote: Fletcher Building (FBU.ASX) returned -10% during the month with the NZ economy remaining in recession and housing construction extremely weak. headline: Spheria warns that momentum has driven small-cap markets away from fundamentals and valuations, but expects a reversion to fundamentals-driven performance
reasoning: The past year saw momentum strategies triumph over fundamental investing in the small-cap market, with stocks experiencing earnings growth bid up with little regard for valuations while cyclical or downgraded businesses fell sharply. quote: The past year marked another year where momentum largely triumphed over logic. The small cap market was marked by a significant uplift in the stocks with earnings growth with scant regard to valuations. Correspondingly, businesses with earnings cyclicality and downgrades plumbed new lows. With apparently fewer investors looking to fundamentals - just ask an ETF or index fund what multiple their underlying investments are trading on – it shouldn't be surprising that things have somewhat disconnected from the economic laws of gravity. Just as a law is a law and not an opinion, however, our view on the weighing ability of the stock market longer term remains intact. Whilst momentum has been the friend of some this year, we have seen the momentum engine slow and reverse previously and have a strong sense of déjà vu.

headline: Spheria's top holding CarGurus rallied +36% in December quarter on strong earnings; remains attractively valued at 17x ex-wholesale EBIT
reasoning: CarGurus is a US online automotive marketplace connecting buyers and sellers of new and used cars, gaining market share in a competitive three-player US market. The stock returned +36% in the quarter following a strong Q3 result that beat expectations on both revenue and earnings, driven by pricing and strong adoption of new dealer efficiency products. CARG is generating ~15% pa top-line growth well ahead of cost growth, resulting in 50%+ earnings growth, and is materially outperforming competitors like Cars.com. Spheria met with management in September 2024 and was impressed by CARG's cheaper pricing, 20% more inventory and 50% more traffic versus competitors. Trading at 24x FY25 EBIT on face value, excluding the loss-making wholesale business (where losses are reducing) brings the multiple to 17x, which Spheria views as very attractive for a share-winning marketplace with net cash and strong cash flow.
quote: CARG is a US online automative marketplace that connects buyers and sellers of new and used cars, much in the same fashion as CarSales (CAR AU) operates in the Australian market. Unlike the Australian market, the US is more competitive, with three major players of roughly equivalent size. CARG has been gaining share and trades at an attractive valuation given the potential for this to continue. The stock returned +36% during the quarter on the back of a strong third quarter result. CARG outperformed market expectations on both revenue and earnings, with pricing the main driver, underpinned by strong adoption of new products that improve dealer efficiency as well as ongoing annual pricing reviews. CARG is generating top line growth of ~15%pa, well in excess of cost growth, resulting in earnings growth of 50%+. Importantly, CARG is materially outperforming its competitors, with Cars.com reporting a comparatively lackluster result for the quarter. The Spheria team met in person with CARG management in September 2024 (along with a key competitor) and came away impressed. What stood out was that CARG offers cheaper pricing than competitors, has 20% more inventory and 50% more traffic, all of which translates into a much better ROI for its dealer customers. Further, the company's obsessive focus on innovation was evident, helping dealerships run their businesses better and be more profitable. CARG is now the largest holding in the fund, reflecting both our conviction in the name and the stock's strong level of outperformance. Trading on a prima facie multiple of 24x FY25 EBIT, CARG doesn't look especially cheap. But excluding the loss-making wholesale business (in which losses are reducing) brings the multiple down to 17x. This is very attractive for a marketplace business that's winning share, generating strong cash flow and has a net cash balance sheet.

headline: Spheria is underweight the US market due to inflated valuations, stock-based compensation distortion, and a benchmark with 63% US weighting
reasoning: Spheria highlights that the MSCI World Small Cap benchmark has a 63% US weighting, making a benchmark-weight allocation imprudent without compelling relative value. The US market trades at a 40-70% premium on forward P/E relative to Japanese, European and UK markets. Additionally, widespread reporting of profits on a pre-SBC basis materially flatters headline multiples, making the US appear cheaper than it truly is — in many cases SBC consumes the entire reported profit. Trump's re-election was seen by markets as net positive due to business-friendly policies, but Spheria is cautious about selective market interpretation of his policy mix. On balance of probabilities, Spheria expects some valuation convergence across regions over the medium term.
quote: So why is the fund underweight the US market? The first thing to highlight is the unusually high weighting in the benchmark to US names. At 63%, a benchmark-weight allocation to the US market would necessitate that two out of every three stocks we owned be domiciled in that market. Whilst the US economy has a lot going for it, such a significant allocation seems imprudent on the face of it, absent compelling value relative to alternate markets. Stock-based compensation (SBC) is a sensible means of aligning employees with shareholders. But make no mistake, it is a real cost for the business. The issuance of stock merely substitutes what was formerly a cash payment of salary for equity dilution. We know of many companies whose entire reported profit is more than consumed by SBC. This has the effect of obscuring value unless one digs into the accounts to understand discrepancies between 'underlying' and statutory results. It also means that headline multiples are significantly flattered, making the US market appear cheaper than it actually is. Even with this unfair advantage, the US market trades at a material premium, ranging from 40% to 70%, on a one-year forward P/E basis relative to the Japanese, European and UK markets. We are the first to acknowledge the limitations of a PE ratio and that expensive assets can always get more expensive. But on the balance of probabilities, we expect some convergence in value across regions over the medium term.

Spending one's time searching for the proverbial needle in the haystack makes little sense to us in the context of an investment universe that's so vast (~8000 companies) and rich with businesses that have observable track records of profits and cash flow. Focusing on businesses with observable track records of generating cash flow and with sound balance sheets tilts the long-term odds in our investors' favour and may just be the closest thing to a free lunch that's available in the global small cap market.

reasoning: Zillow underperformed after the National Association of Realtors announced a US$418m settlement designed to promote more transparent buyer-agent commission structures. Spheria believes the most likely outcome is little to no impact on Zillow's revenue, noting that 13 states have already operated under a similar model with no observable impact. Fewer commission dollars could actually make Zillow more valuable to productive agents, driving up lead prices. Longer term, Spheria sees potential for the US to shift from a lead-gen to a paid-inclusion model similar to REA Group in Australia, with Zillow capturing more of the economics. On a market cap per capita basis, Zillow would be worth 26x more than its current price if valued like REA Group, though Spheria acknowledges this is not its base case.
quote: Whilst this may negatively impact the aggregate size of the agent commission pool (from which Zillow's earns its revenue), the most likely outcome in our view is little to no impact on Zillow. Notably 13 states have operated for a few years under a model similar to what's proposed under the settlement, with no observable impact on Zillow's revenue. Indeed, fewer dollars to go around for buyer's agents could actually make Zillow more valuable for the most productive agents, driving up the price of leads. Longer-term, there is some prospect that these changes ultimately pave the way for US to move from a 'lead-gen' to a 'paid inclusion' model like the one that we see in Australia, with the role of aggregating buyers shifting from the buyers agents to Zillow, in turn allowing Zillow to capture more of the economics. Whilst not our base case and the following analysis is admittedly crude, on a market capitalization per capita basis, Zillow would be worth 26x more than the current share price were it to be valued like REA Group (REA.AX).

headline: Spheria expects RBA easing bias to emerge late 2024 as domestic inflation continues to trend lower
reasoning: Spheria argues that the Covid-era inflationary surge was a coordinated super-inflationary event that has since been largely unwound. Monetary tightening, higher rates, and economic reopening have drained excess global liquidity and normalised supply chains. China is now experiencing deflation (CPI -0.5% YoY, PPI -3% YoY). While Australian consumers are struggling and retailers face tough conditions, housing prices remain strong and unemployment is low — mixed signals for the RBA. Spheria expects an easing bias to emerge late in 2024 assuming domestic inflation continues to trend downward.
quote: What drove this appears to have been the confluence of several factors – firstly valuations were low in all of the names attracting bids, secondly there is now a building consensus that interest rates are likely to have peaked in the US and not far off their peak in Australia. We support this view on the basis that the remarkable events around Covid ended up being a co-ordinated super inflationary event which has since been unwound. The monetary tightening globally, higher interest rates and the re-opening of economies has seen a lot of excess liquidity drained from global economies and production bottlenecks unwind. Supply chains have largely normalised. In China we are seeing deflation – yes you read that correctly – deflation with consumer prices down 0.5% YoY and producer prices (the prices manufacturers broadly charge for goods) down 3% YoY. Consumers are struggling in Australia with retailers reporting very tough trading environments, however, housing prices remain strong and unemployment relatively low. These are confusing signals for the RBA to interpret. headline: Spheria warns of extreme valuation disconnect and forced selling in smaller companies creating a micro-cap 'Twilight Zone'
reasoning: Spheria observes that markets, particularly at the smaller-company end, have entered an unusual environment with extreme valuation disconnects between growth and value stocks. Money is clearly exiting the smaller end of the market, driven by a flight to safety and industry funds exiting mandates given their increased size. Selling and lack of risk appetite has led to extremely large drawdowns for anything with a negative earnings delta, accentuated for companies with any debt regardless of cash flow adequacy. Companies that have addressed these issues via capital raisings or asset sales still face persistent valuation stigma.
quote: Many parts of the sharemarket especially the smaller company end have entered something resembling the 'Twilight Zone' where unusual phenomena are so frequent that nothing really surprises us anymore. Case in point being the extreme disconnect in valuations between 'growth' and 'value' companies where the definition of each is simply a gauge of popularity or unpopularity in the case of value. Money is also clearly exiting the smaller end whether it be a flight to safety or industry funds exiting mandates given the marginal incremental contribution to performance given their increased size. The selling in certain names and the lack of risk appetite has meant extremely large drawdowns for anything resembling a negative earnings delta. This has been accentuated in anything that has debt regardless of whether the company's cash flow can support that debt.

headline: Up 12% in September on oil price strength; two conventional oil fields returning $150m+ to shareholders over three years, still trading at 18c vs 4c entry
reasoning: Horizon Oil rose over 12% in September on the back of a strengthening oil price. quote: Horizon Oil (HZN.ASX) share price rose over 12% in September on the back of a strengthening oil price. For those not familiar with HZN, it has substantial interests in two conventional oil fields. The larger one being in the Beibu Gulf (off China) which has produced around 10k barrels of oil per day (bopd) on a gross basis for the last ten years and is forecast to do so for at least a further six years. The other being Maari that is off New Zealand and has produced around 5k bopd which has at least another 4 years of production at or around these levels. When we first acquired our position in HZN about 7 years ago it was trading around 4c and facing numerous issues including too much debt and serious corruption allegations in respect of its PNG gas assets, which were subsequently divested. headline: Spheria believes the market has massively overreacted to Link Administration's HESTA client loss and sees significant recovery potential in its core share registry and superannuation administration businesses
reasoning: Spheria bought into LNK late in the prior calendar year after a significant retracement driven by legal proceedings in its UK Funds Solutions division (LFSL). With LFSL divested and a compensation scheme in place, the company is left with Link Market Services (share registry, second largest in AU/NZ) and RSS (largest superannuation administrator in the industry fund space in Australia). The loss of HESTA (~10% of RSS revenue) to Growsuper spooked the market in July and August, but Spheria argues transitioning a large account is akin to moving a Big 4 bank to a new software platform and that major clients are more likely to renegotiate terms than leave. There is also uncertainty around whether Growsuper can successfully scale from a low base to over 1 million accounts.
quote: We bought into LNK late last calendar year after a significant retracement in the share price due primarily to several legal proceedings relating to its Funds Solutions (LFSL) division in the UK. With this now on the path to full resolution due to divestment of LFSL and a scheme which will provide compensation to those clients affected, the business is now left with two core divisions being Link Market Services (share registry and employee share plans) and Retirement & Superannuation Solutions (RSS) which provides administration services to large superannuation funds. Both businesses are large players in their industry verticals with Link Market Services the second largest player in Australia and NZ, third in the UK and second in India, whilst RSS is the largest administrator in the industry fund space in Australia. Unfortunately, at the end of June RSS lost a large client (HESTA) representing ~10% of divisional revenue to Growsuper. This raised the specter of further larger client losses and routed the share price in July and August, with some relief in September. We believe the market has massively overreacted to this news given the complexity of transitioning a large account is akin to moving a "Big 4 bank to a new software platform" as one industry expert opined.

headline: Constructive on Australian smaller companies, expecting M&A surge and a wall of capital inflows as interest rates peak and migration drives population growth
reasoning: Spheria sees the dislocation between value and price in small companies at historic highs, which it expects will drive a significant pickup in M&A activity from both strategic buyers and private equity over the next 6-12 months. The firm also notes that strong immigration-driven population growth and superannuation contribution rates rising to 12% from July 2025 are structural tailwinds. A peak in interest rates could catalyse a large reallocation of capital back into equities, with smaller companies likely to outperform given how neglected they have been. The firm draws a parallel to the rapid re-rating of beaten-up tech stocks in the prior quarter as a reminder of how quickly these moves can occur.
quote: With the dislocation between value and price in small companies at historic highs, we expect M&A activity to ramp up even further over the next 6 - 12 months. Strategic buyers and private equity alike have a demonstrated propensity to take advantage of depressed valuations and a willingness to take a longer-term view than many other market participants. This is but one way that value ultimately gets realised, supporting our conviction that remaining true to our investment process will deliver just rewards. In recent times we have witnessed a huge asset allocation away from equities and fund manager's hoarding cash, all in anticipation of a "buy the correction moment". This has helped to drive a wedge between large and smaller cap performance, in our view. But with the Australian population set to grow strongly next year due to decade high levels of migration and superannuation contribution rates increasing to 12% from July 2025, a peak in interest rates could see an epic wall of capital flood back into equities, a backdrop that is almost certain to see smaller companies outperform.

headline: Held despite profit warning and near 3-year-low price; thesis intact but regret not anticipating market's harsh reaction to cyclical earnings peak; H1 revenue 15-20% below prior year, full-year earnings US$36m vs consensus
reasoning: Somero issued a trading update guiding H1 revenue to be 15-20% below the prior year and full-year revenue around 10% lower, driven by elevated interest rates, tightened bank lending standards and construction permitting delays. Full-year earnings are expected at US$36m, 16% below market consensus. The company is cutting its workforce by 10% and managing down inventory. The market reacted sharply with a 12% immediate decline followed by a further 8% drop in subsequent weeks, leaving the stock trading near a 3-year low and more than halved from its January 2022 peak. The fund acknowledges the likelihood of earnings peaking was built into their forecasts given the cyclical nature of non-residential construction, but regrets not being more alert to how the market would react to a cyclical business moving past its earnings peak. The fund retains conviction in Somero as the clear industry innovator with 20+ products protected by 100+ patents and a dominant position in laser screed technology.
quote: Somero (SOM LN) – Issued a trading update during the month in which it said that it expects revenue in the first half to be 15-20% below the prior year comparative due to factors affecting the US market, with full year revenue expected to be around 10% lower than the prior year. Factors cited were elevated interest rates, tightened bank lending standards and, to a lesser degree, construction permitting delays. In response, the company is reducing its operational workforce by 10% and will manage down inventory levels. Full year earnings are expected to be US$36m or 16% below market consensus. The market's response was swift and unforgiving, with an immediate 12% share price decline, followed by a further 8% in the following weeks. At the time of writing, Somero is trading near its 3-year low and has more than halved from its Jan-22 peak. Somero pioneered the laser screed machine in 1986. It's patented, laser-guided technology automates the process of laying concrete slabs for commercial flooring and provides a high level of precision at a significantly higher rate of efficiency. Somero's products are productivity and quality enhancers for its concrete contractor customers. It is the clear industry innovator, offering more than 20 products protected by over 100 patents.

quote: Spheria originally purchased Pointsbet on the announcement of the sale of the US business, which has been cash-burning for several years in pursuit of market share gains in a highly competitive market against players with far deeper pockets. There are not many ways to get leverage to AI in the Australian listed market outside of Appen and with a refreshed management team already making inroads as demonstrated at the investor day in May we are confident of what lies ahead for this business. Appen is well placed to benefit from the growth in generative AI which requires human input, particularly as it relates to ensuring the accuracy of the outputs. Appen has been pivoting towards Large Language Model (LLM) type work with the expectation that this market will grow to more than $100bn by 2030. The recent capital raise provides ample funds to invest in the growth of the business for the next couple of years. A substantial US$300m of revenue (admittedly vs a peak of around >US$400m) alongside a re-engineered cost base will mean the business achieves profitability in the short to medium term. On a price to revenue metric the company is trading on less than 1x. Assuming the business can generate 10% EBIT margins (not a stretch in our view) it would be generating US$30m of EBIT and trading on a modest 10x EV/EBIT.

headline: Portfolio construction skewed to ~70% net cash balance sheets as protection against cyclical downturns and to preserve optionality to acquire over-geared competitors near cycle troughs
reasoning: The fund holds approximately 70% of its positions in companies with net cash balance sheets. The rationale is that debt is the only mechanism through which a company can go bankrupt, so a strong balance sheet protects against being forced out of positions during cyclical downturns. Additionally, net cash positions provide optionality at cycle troughs to acquire over-leveraged competitors or invest organically to widen competitive moats. Excessive leverage is particularly dangerous when combined with weak competitive positioning and regulatory dependence, as illustrated by the US regional bank failures. The strategy is designed to reduce the impact of losses on performance and tilt the playing field in favour of long-term investors.
quote: Across the fund, around 70% of our holdings have net cash balance sheets. Debt is not inherently 'bad'. Indeed the application of leverage can improve the process of capital allocation across an economy, resulting in a net gain in productive investment. In addition, the benefits and risks of leverage are symmetrical, with the magnification of returns a feature on the positive as well as the negative side of the ledger. However, it's at the individual company level where the reasons for our scrutiny on the balance sheet come into focus. The benefits of a strong balance sheet can be summarised as follows: You can't get 'stopped out' by a cyclical downturn in operations. The only way a company can go broke is if it has debt; and - Optionality – At or near the bottom of the cycle, this may include the ability to buy over-geared competitors and/or to invest organically in the company's own operations as a means of widening its moat.

quote: US regional banks fail to meet our investment criteria on multiple fronts. By definition this places the regional banks at a disadvantage to their larger peers. Softer regulations were an attempt by US regulators to level the playing field. Weaker risk controls (aided by the softer regulatory requirements), rising interest rates, and a concentration of lending activities to cash-strapped segments of the economy (crypto and tech) all contributed to what was a spectacular collapse. reasoning: Napco's competitive advantage stems from its culture of innovation (dozens of patents) and vertically integrated end-to-end solutions across alarms, locking and access control, delivering superior reliability. quote: A key inflection point for the business occurred 7-8 years ago when Napco seized on the looming decommissioning of the copper phone networks to introduce a recurring revenue product to its suite. Historically the signal from Napco's products (alarm, fire etc) was transmitted through the telecommunication provider's copper networks to a central station, where the appropriate authorities were notified, and the appropriate course of action taken. With the decommissioning of the US copper networks, Napco's cellular radio-capable products now route the signal to the central station via Napco's own Network Operations Centre (NOC). For this service, the company receives a $10-$25/month fee. Whilst the stock is not outright cheap on earnings multiples, it has strong cash flow and returns, no debt, and continues to be well-placed to benefit from several growth drivers, including the increasing focus on school safety, regulatory mandated fire alarm upgrades, and copper phone line obsolescence, which will help to drive high value recurring revenue for signal transmission over Napco's cellular infrastructure.

quote: Hemnet (HEM SS) – As Sweden's largest real estate portal, Hemnet has greater than 10x the revenue and monthly visitation than its nearest competitor, making it more dominant than the leading portals in the USA, UK, Germany and Australia. Evidence abounds of how hard it is to dislodge a market leading real estate portal. Like any marketplace, volume begets volume. Indeed the network effects are arguably more powerful for real estate portals than for the average marketplace given that buying a home is one of the most significant financial transactions that the end customer will ever make. This characteristic lend itself to a winner-takes-all/most industry structure, as the cost (perceived or otherwise) of not advertising where the most eyeballs reside can be significant. Like most of the markets we look at, Swedish home buyers are retreating in the face of higher interest rates, with Hemnet reporting a 10% decline in fourth quarter listing volumes vs the prior corresponding period. Notwithstanding this, listing price increases in excess of 30% are helping to deliver revenue growth and higher margins. This is an unusually stark demonstration of a company exercising its pricing power. For context, Hemnet is relatively early on the journey of monetising its dominance, evidenced by comparatively low listing prices (both in absolute terms and as a percentage of house prices) in comparison to other market leading real estate portals. With a capable management team, a board populated by ex-Realestate.com.au and ex-Rightmove executives, and its sheer dominance, we remain confident in the long-term prospects of this business.

The business recently sold its Main Event business for US$835m (AU$957m) with a deferred consideration of up to US$14.8m. headline: Market has flipped from paying any price to own certain stocks to accepting any price not to own them — creating opportunities for longer-term, fundamentals-based investors
reasoning: The sentiment shift from growth-at-any-price to fear-driven selling is creating mispriced opportunities in the small cap space. Margin pressures and top-line deferrals are causing outsized negative share price reactions. Fundamentals-based investors with a longer time horizon can exploit these dislocations.
quote: Whereas we were in a market where people would pay any price to OWN certain stocks, we have shifted to a market in which some people will ACCEPT any price NOT to own certain stocks. This flip in view can create opportunities for longer term and more fundamentally based investors.

headline: Bond yield declines driving equity rally; inflation pressures easing faster than expected, but real economy still slowing under rate rises and energy cost pressures
reasoning: November's strong global equity performance was largely driven by falling 10-year bond yields as inflation pressures eased. Forces driving inflation down include falling commodity prices, unwind of extreme goods trade pressure post-COVID, and falling shipping and production costs in Asia. The real economy is expected to continue slowing in reaction to rate rises and energy supply decisions. Companies are warning of margin pressures and deferrals in top-line spending, which is causing outsized share price reactions and creating opportunities in small caps.
quote: The rebound appears to be largely driven by 10-year bond yields falling on the back of generally reducing pressures on inflation. We have been suggesting that there were many forces likely to drive inflation down including falling commodity prices, an unwind of the extreme pressure on goods trade (driven by the Covid surge followed by massive overstocking in the retail system globally) which in turn was driving down shipping and production costs in Asia. This has started to manifest in reported numbers which has got people thinking about when the current rates cycle may peak – possibly sooner and at a lower peak than previously thought. Our sense is that the real economy will continue to slow in reaction to rate rises and some decisions around energy supply which are now causing system wide price increases.
